Kenya_2026-08-15_weekly_precip: ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 15 to 22 August is confined to the west along the Uganda border and the Lake Victoria basin (15 to 25 mm) and to the south coast (12 to 20 mm), with the north and centre of Kenya below 5 mm. The same west and coast pattern holds through 12 September with little change in amounts. From 12 to 26 September totals rise to 25 to 35 mm at the western edge of the domain and to 20 to 25 mm on the coast, and 35 to 45 mm appear north of 5N in southern Ethiopia.
Kenya_2026-08-15_gefs_weekly_precip: GEFS puts a localized maximum of 30 to 45 mm over the western highlands between 1.5N and 1S for 15 to 22 August, with about 10 mm on the south coast and virtually no rain elsewhere. From 22 August to 12 September the western maximum weakens to 15 to 30 mm along the Uganda border and the coast receives 10 to 18 mm per week. For 12 to 19 September the west drops to 8 to 15 mm while the south coast near 4.5S increases to 15 to 25 mm.
Kenya_2026-08-15_weekly_precip_downscale: Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 15 to 22 August is 25 to 40 mm in the west between the Uganda border and about 36E, and 15 to 30 mm in a narrow strip along the coast, with the rest of the country dry. The western maximum stays above 40 mm near the equator through 12 September and the coastal strip holds 20 to 35 mm. From 12 to 26 September the west intensifies into a broad area above 40 mm from Lake Victoria to 35.5E, and in the week of 19 to 26 September more than 40 mm is also indicated on the north coast and its hinterland.
Kenya_2026-08-15_weekly_medium_range_pre: The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 15 to 22 August has scattered totals of 20 to 35 mm over the west and southwest between 1.5N and 1S, 12 to 20 mm over the southeast coast, and less than 5 mm across the north and centre. For 22 to 29 August the western maximum strengthens to 25 to 35 mm along the Uganda border from 3N to the equator, with isolated cells above 30 mm near the southern border around 3S and on the south coast. The north-central and eastern interior stay dry in both weeks.
Kenya_2026-08-15_chance_of_above_or_belo: A sharp west to east contrast marks 15 to 22 August, with a below-normal lean of -75 to -100 points over the northwest and north-centre and an above-normal lean of +75 to +100 points in the east and northeast along the Somali border and the coast. The below-normal lean of -60 to -100 points persists over the west and northwest through 12 September, while the east and coast stay at +40 to +75 points. From 12 to 26 September the western signal weakens to -30 to -70 points and the eastern above-normal lean holds.
Kenya_2026-08-15_efi_sot_precip: Only a weak wet-extreme signal is present for 15 to 22 August, with EFI values of 0.55 to 0.65 in the northeast along the Somali and Ethiopian borders between 0.5N and 4.5N and in one cell near the southern border around 3S, and almost no supporting SOT contour. For 22 to 29 August isolated cells of 0.55 to 0.65 remain on the coast near 3S and south of the border near 4.5S. No EFI shading above 0.5 appears from 5 September onward, although a SOT zero contour covers the coast and the east for 19 to 26 September.
Kenya_2026-08-15_50th_percentile_exedanc: The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 15 to 22 August is below 10% across the northwest and north-centre but 90 to 100% in the east and northeast and near the southern border around 37.5E. The west and northwest stay at 1 to 25% through 12 September, while the east holds 55 to 90%, highest along the Somali border and the coast. From 12 to 26 September the northwest recovers slightly to 10 to 45% and the coast near 3S reaches 90 to 99%.
Kenya_2026-08-15_anomaly_from_50th: The ensemble mean for 15 to 22 August is 10 to 15 mm below the model-climate median in the west and northwest and 5 to 12 mm above it on the coast and in the northeast. The deficit deepens to 15 to 23 mm in the west near Lake Victoria on the equator from 22 August to 12 September, with a small surplus of 5 to 12 mm on the coast near 3S. From 12 to 26 September the deficit is limited to the cell west of 35E on the equator, while surpluses of 10 to 18 mm develop on the north coast and 5 to 10 mm over the east.
